compoundNote: Nicotinamide riboside (NR) is a form of vitamin B3 and an NAD+ precursor; supplements usually contain the synthetic salt nicotinamide riboside chloride (NRC), sold as NIAGEN / TRU NIAGEN by Niagen Bioscience (formerly ChromaDex). Human trials in this snapshot dose by mass of NR chloride where they say so (Trammell 2016, Conze 2019), which makes a 250 mg NRC label directly comparable to trial doses. NooCube NAD+ label: 1 capsule daily, 250 mg nicotinamide riboside chloride, 30 servings. Only trials of NR itself are listed in studies[]; trials of NMN, niacin, nicotinamide and multi-ingredient products are not evidence for NR (the NR + pterostilbene trial, PMID 29184669, is included only because it is the sole controlled trial near 250 mg/day and is flagged as a combination). Headline: NR reliably raises blood NAD+ in humans (a biomarker), but the randomized trials that tested thinking, memory, fatigue or disease outcomes (all in MCI, long-COVID, Parkinson's or PAD, at 1,000 to 3,000 mg/day) found no cognitive benefit, and the largest, NOPARK (n=410, PMID 42848371), found worse outcomes than placebo in Parkinson's. No cognition RCT was found in healthy adults. Much NR research is funded or supplied by ChromaDex/Niagen Bioscience or Elysium Health. All pubmedUrl status values are 203 because NCBI served a bot-challenge page to curl; see statusNote.

verdicts.claim: Raises NAD+ in human blood (biomarker, not a health outcome)
verdicts.reason: Replicated across independent placebo-controlled human trials: whole-blood NAD+ +22% / +51% / +142% at 100 / 300 / 1,000 mg/day for 8 weeks (Conze 2019, n=140, PMID 31278280); PBMC NAD+ about +60% at 1,000 mg/day for 6 weeks (Martens 2018, PMID 29599478); about 2-fold or 2.6-fold at 1,000 mg/day in MCI trials (PMIDs 37994989, 42478598); 2.6-3.1-fold at 2,000 mg/day (PMID 41357333); about +40% for 250 mg NR plus pterostilbene (PMID 29184669). Nat Metab 2026 (PMID 41540253) reproduces it over 14 days in adults of mean age 34.7. Caveats: most trials are ChromaDex/Niagen- or Elysium-linked; the magnitude varies widely between people (PMID 41858901); the 250 mg daily dose has not been tested as NR alone with NAD+ as an outcome. Blood NAD+ is a surrogate; none of these papers shows that raising it improves how people feel or think.

verdicts.claim: Improves cognition or memory in healthy adults
verdicts.reason: No randomized trial of NR with a cognitive primary outcome in healthy adults was found in the PubMed searches run (see notes for the queries). The healthy-adult trials measured NAD+ metabolites, blood pressure, muscle or vascular outcomes. Evidence of benefit is therefore absent rather than negative. The only cognitive-adjacent healthy-adult data are surrogate: NR lowered Abeta42, pJNK and pERK1/2 in neuron-enriched extracellular vesicles in 22 older adults (PMID 36515353), with no cognitive test reported. Mechanistic and rodent cognition claims do not carry over to people.

verdicts.claim: Cognition in mild cognitive impairment / subjective cognitive decline (disease population)
verdicts.reason: Direction: null so far. Three small randomized placebo-controlled trials gave NR (1,000 mg/day, 8-12 weeks, n=20 to about 46) and each found no cognitive improvement on its primary or main cognitive outcome (MoCA, PMID 37994989; RBANS, PMID 39817194; primary cognitive outcome, PMID 42478598), even though blood NAD+ rose 2- to 2.6-fold. Exploratory signals - lower plasma pTau217 (-7% vs +18%, p=0.02, PMID 39817194), regional cerebral blood flow changes in both PMID 37994989 (reduced default-mode CBF, not significant after correction) and PMID 42478598 (hippocampal increase, exploratory) - are inconsistent and are not cognitive benefits. The meta-analysis of muscle function reported slower chair-stand and lower SPPB in NR-treated MCI (PMID 40275690). A 2024 systematic review calling the AD evidence promising (PMID 39422945) rests on two human trials the abstract does not name. Keep disease findings separate from healthy-adult claims.

Grade is for the evidence base; direction is AGAINST benefit. Two small early trials were positive-leaning (NADPARK, n=30, PMID 35235774: variable brain NAD rise and 'mild clinical improvement'; NR-SAFE, n=20, 3,000 mg/day, PMID 38016950: MDS-UPDRS improved but confounded by levodopa timing). The definitive phase 3 NOPARK trial (n=410, 1,000 mg/day, 52 weeks, JAMA 2026, PMID 42848371) found MDS-UPDRS worse on NR than placebo (+2.72 points, p=.02) and worse non-motor symptoms, and concluded NR does not support disease-modifying use. Do not present NR as neuroprotective for Parkinson's.

verdicts.claim: Reduces fatigue or raises mental energy
verdicts.reason: Only one randomized trial with a fatigue outcome was found: long-COVID, 2,000 mg/day, n=58, where the Fatigue Severity Scale did not differ from placebo (p=0.59, PMID 41357333); post-hoc within-group improvements are unadjusted and exploratory, and dropout reached 51% by 20 weeks. No trial in healthy or fatigued-but-otherwise-healthy adults was found. A meta-analysis of physical function found no support for NR/NMN in people over 60 (PMID 40275690). Nothing here supports a 'mental energy' claim.

verdicts.claim: Anti-aging / healthspan benefit from raising NAD+
verdicts.reason: A critical review of 25 human NR studies concluded oral NR 'has displayed few clinically relevant effects' and that the literature tends to exaggerate (PMID 37478182). A 2026 PRISMA systematic review (33 human studies) found consistent target engagement but functional and healthspan effects 'heterogeneous and often null', and called clinical effectiveness for anti-aging or wellness 'inconclusive' (PMID 41655607). No human trial measured aging outcomes (mortality, disease incidence, validated biological-age endpoints beyond exploratory methylation clocks in 20 MCI patients, PMID 37994989).

verdicts.claim: Safety at 100-1,000 mg/day for weeks to months in adults
verdicts.reason: No significant excess of adverse events versus placebo in the controlled trials at 100-1,000 mg/day for 8 weeks (Conze, n=140, PMID 31278280) and at 1,000 mg/day for 8-12 weeks in older adults and MCI (PMIDs 39817194, 42478598), and no moderate or severe AEs at 3,000 mg/day for 4 weeks in 20 people with Parkinson's (PMID 38016950). EFSA judged NR chloride safe up to 300 mg/day for healthy adults (230 mg/day in pregnancy and lactation) (PMID 32626405). Limits: longest RCT is 52 weeks and was in Parkinson's, where outcomes were worse on NR (PMID 42848371); healthy-adult trials are 8 weeks or less; EFSA's 2021 opinion flags experimental pathways for harm at high intakes (PMID 34804232).

doseAssessment.trialRange: Biomarker trials: single doses 100 / 300 / 1,000 mg (Trammell 2016, n=12, PMID 27721479); 100 / 300 / 1,000 mg/day for 8 weeks (Conze 2019, n=140, PMID 31278280) giving whole-blood NAD+ +22% / +51% / +142%; 1,000 mg/day for 6 weeks (Martens 2018, PMID 29599478) and 21 days (Elhassan 2019, PMID 31412242); 1,000 mg/day for 14 days (PMID 41540253); 250 mg NR plus 50 mg pterostilbene and 500 mg plus 100 mg daily for 8 weeks (PMID 29184669, combination product, +40% and +90%). Airhart 2017 (PMID 29211728) used 250 mg on days 1-2 only before titrating to 2,000 mg/day, and did not report NAD+ at that step. Cognition / functional trials (all disease populations): 1,000 mg/day (PMIDs 37994989, 42478598, 39817194, 35235774, 42848371), 2,000 mg/day (long-COVID, PMID 41357333), 3,000 mg/day (Parkinson's safety, PMID 38016950). No cognitive trial used NR below 1,000 mg/day, and no cognitive RCT in healthy adults was found. Trial doses are stated as mg of NR chloride (NIAGEN) where the papers say so (PMIDs 27721479, 31278280), so a 250 mg nicotinamide riboside chloride label is comparable to those figures.
doseAssessment.suggestedText: For raising blood NAD+, 250 mg per day of nicotinamide riboside chloride sits inside the range that has been tested (100 to 1,000 mg per day and above): a dose-ranging trial found whole-blood NAD+ up 22% at 100 mg and 51% at 300 mg after 8 weeks, and a combination product with 250 mg of NR raised it about 40%. We found no trial of 250 mg of NR alone with blood NAD+ as the outcome, so the exact effect at that dose is interpolated, not measured. For thinking, memory or energy, 250 mg is well below every dose that has been studied: trials with cognitive or fatigue outcomes used 1,000 to 3,000 mg per day, all in people with mild cognitive impairment, Parkinson's disease or long-COVID, and none showed a cognitive benefit. There is no evidence that 250 mg per day improves cognition or energy. EFSA assessed up to 300 mg per day of NR chloride as safe for healthy adults.

safetySignals.signal: NOPARK phase 3 (1,000 mg/day, 52 weeks, early Parkinson's, n=410): MDS-UPDRS total scores were worse on NR than placebo (+2.72 points, p=.02) and non-motor symptoms worsened more on NR (NMSS +4.22, p=.009). Serious adverse events were fewer on NR (8.3% vs 14.1%). Relevant to anyone with Parkinson's or on levodopa; mechanism unknown.
safetySignals.title: Nicotinamide Riboside for Patients With Early-Stage Parkinson Disease: The NOPARK Randomized Clinical Trial

safetySignals.signal: Long-COVID RCT (2,000 mg/day): dropout in the NR-NR arm was 32.4% at 10 weeks and 51.4% at 20 weeks vs 14.3% in the placebo-first arm; the abstract does not give reasons for dropout. One serious adverse event, judged unrelated to NR.
safetySignals.title: Effects of nicotinamide riboside on NAD+ levels, cognition, and symptom recovery in long-COVID: a randomized controlled trial

safetySignals.signal: NR-SAFE (3,000 mg/day, 4 weeks, Parkinson's, n=20): no moderate or severe adverse events, but a slight initial rise in serum homocysteine on NR; the authors judged the methyl-donor pool intact and recommend safety monitoring in higher-dose trials.
safetySignals.title: NR-SAFE: a randomized, double-blind safety trial of high dose nicotinamide riboside in Parkinson's disease

safetySignals.signal: Conze 2019 (100, 300, 1,000 mg/day, 8 weeks, n=140): no significant difference in adverse events between NR and placebo or across doses, no flushing, no LDL-cholesterol rise, no 1-carbon dysregulation. Seven participants did not finish (one placebo withdrawal for nausea). Healthy-adult safety data stop at 8 weeks.
safetySignals.title: Safety and Metabolism of Long-term Administration of NIAGEN (Nicotinamide Riboside Chloride) in a Randomized, Double-Blind, Placebo-controlled Clinical Trial of Healthy Overweight Adults

safetySignals.signal: EFSA (2019) concluded NR chloride is safe at up to 300 mg/day for healthy adults, excluding pregnant and lactating women, for whom only up to 230 mg/day was judged safe because the margin of exposure from a rat developmental study (76) was below 100. People who are pregnant or breastfeeding are therefore outside the supported range at 250 mg/day.
safetySignals.title: Safety of nicotinamide riboside chloride as a novel food pursuant to Regulation (EU) 2015/2283 and bioavailability of nicotinamide from this source, in the context of Directive 2002/46/EC

safetySignals.signal: EFSA (2021) extension-of-use opinion could not establish safety for NR chloride in meal-replacement products and nutritional drink mixes at 300 mg/day for the general population (infant exposure margins), and notes 'experimental data which indicate several pathways by which intakes of nicotinamide (or its precursors), at levels that are substantially higher than the physiological requirement, might cause adverse effects', suggesting the nicotinamide UL may need re-evaluation.
safetySignals.title: Extension of use of nicotinamide riboside chloride as a novel food pursuant to Regulation (EU) 2015/2283

safetySignals.signal: Animal toxicology (rats, not human): 90-day NR study, NOAEL 300 mg/kg/day, LOAEL 1,000 mg/kg/day, target organs liver, kidney, ovaries and testes at high doses, similar toxicity profile to equimolar nicotinamide.
safetySignals.title: Safety assessment of nicotinamide riboside, a form of vitamin B(3)

safetySignals.signal: Mouse-only signal, no human equivalent found: NAD+ boosting (including NR) increased atherosclerotic plaque and inflammation in Apoe knockout mice. Human cardiovascular relevance is untested.
safetySignals.title: NAD(+) boosting increases atherosclerotic plaques and inflammation in Apoe knockout mice

safetySignals.signal: Heart-failure pilot (1,000 mg twice daily, n=30): appeared safe and well tolerated and about doubled whole-blood NAD+ (disease population, high dose).
safetySignals.title: Safety and Tolerability of Nicotinamide Riboside in Heart Failure With Reduced Ejection Fraction

gaps: No randomized trial with a cognitive, memory or attention primary outcome in healthy adults was found for nicotinamide riboside. The cognition trials are all in disease populations (MCI/SCD, long-COVID, Parkinson's, PAD), at 1,000 to 3,000 mg/day, and none showed a cognitive benefit on its primary outcome.

No trial of NR alone at about 250 mg/day with blood NAD+ as an outcome was found. The nearest is the 250 mg NR + 50 mg pterostilbene combination (PMID 29184669, Elysium-funded) and the 100 / 300 mg arms of Conze 2019 (PMID 31278280); the effect at 250 mg is interpolated.

No NooCube-specific data: no study of the NooCube NAD+ product itself was searched for or found; the evidence here is about NR chloride in general (mostly NIAGEN / TruNiagen supplied by ChromaDex/Niagen Bioscience). Whether NooCube's source and purity match the trial material is not verified.

Fatigue / mental energy: the only controlled fatigue outcome is the long-COVID trial (null, PMID 41357333). No trial in healthy people or in fatigue syndromes (e.g. ME/CFS) was found; a ME/CFS review (PMID 35656104) was seen in search results but is a mechanistic review, not trial evidence, and was not appraised.

Most NR trials are small (8 to 140 participants), short (14 days to 12 weeks) and funded, supplied or co-authored by ChromaDex/Niagen Bioscience or Elysium Health; independent replication of the NAD+ rise exists (e.g. Nestle, PMID 41540253) but independent cognitive trials are all null. Funding for several trials (PMIDs 35235774, 38016950, 42848371, 41858901, 41540253) was not verified from the abstract.
Dose of the PAD pilot (PMID 40479886) could not be verified from the abstract or the PMC page text retrieved; its cognitive 'improvements' are from 8 open-label participants with no control.

Long-term safety in healthy people is not established: the longest RCT is 52 weeks (Parkinson's, worse outcomes on NR), healthy-adult safety trials stop at 8 weeks, and EFSA flagged that the nicotinamide upper intake level may need re-evaluation (PMID 34804232).

Context only, not NR-alone evidence: the combined-metabolic-activators trial in Alzheimer's disease (PMID 36703196, n and per-ingredient effect not isolated) gave 1 g NR as one of four ingredients (L-serine, NR, N-acetylcysteine, L-carnitine tartrate) and reported ADAS-Cog improvement; the NR contribution cannot be separated and the authors are ScandiBio Therapeutics founders. It is listed here, not in studies[], for that reason.

Context only: an in-vitro study in Alzheimer's-patient fibroblasts and iPSC-derived cells found NR plus caffeine partly restored NAD but not energy metabolism (PMID 35730144) - cell data, not human trial evidence.

Vendor anti-aging claims were not assessed against the vendor page; this snapshot covers PubMed evidence only. No human trial of NR measured aging endpoints (lifespan, disease incidence, validated biological-age outcomes).

The official pubmedUrl check could not return HTTP 200 from curl (NCBI returns a 203 challenge page for all 28 cited PMIDs); PMIDs, titles, journals and years were verified via E-utilities esummary (HTTP 200).

Searches may have missed trials indexed without the words 'nicotinamide riboside' in the title/abstract, trials published after 2026-10-19, and non-English reports; ClinicalTrials.gov was not searched for unpublished completed trials.
